what_its_for: This gel is used to treat acne (pimples and blackheads) on your face, chest, or back. Adapalene helps unclog pores and reduces inflammation, while benzoyl peroxide kills the bacteria that cause acne. Together, they help clear existing breakouts and prevent new ones from forming.
how_to_take: Wash your hands before and after applying this gel. Gently wash the affected skin area with a mild soap or cleanser, then pat dry. Apply a thin layer of gel to the entire affected area — not just on individual pimples — once daily in the evening or at bedtime. Avoid getting the gel in your eyes, mouth, lips, nostrils, or on broken or sunburned skin. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not use more than directed — using extra will not clear acne faster and may cause more irritation.
dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected area ONCE daily, preferably in the evening or at bedtime. Use only a pea-sized amount for the face. Do not apply more than once a day unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and apply your next dose at the regular time. Never apply a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tube or pump tightly closed when not in use. Keep away from heat, open flames, and direct sunlight, as benzoyl peroxide is flammable. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid spending long periods in the sun or using tanning beds while using this medication, as it makes your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Always apply a broad-spectrum sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher) and wear protective clothing when going outdoors. Avoid using other harsh or drying skin products, such as medicated soaps, astringents, toners with alcohol, or other acne treatments, at the same time unless your doctor approves. Avoid waxing, threading, or using hair removal products on treated skin. This gel can bleach hair, clothing, towels, and bed linens — let it dry completely before contact with fabrics.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or pharmacist if you experience: severe redness, peeling, swelling, blistering, or burning of the skin; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; severe skin irritation that does not improve after a few weeks; or if your acne gets significantly worse. Also call your doctor before using this medication if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
when_it_works: Do not expect overnight results. Most people start to see some improvement in their acne after 1 to 2 weeks, but it may take 8 to 12 weeks (about 2 to 3 months) of regular use to see the full benefit. Your acne may briefly appear slightly worse in the first few weeks — this is normal. Keep using the gel as directed even if you do not see immediate results.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Adapalene may be harmful to an unborn baby. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor before using this product. If you are breastfeeding, consult your doctor before use and avoid applying it near the chest area to prevent the baby from coming into contact with the medication. Children: This medication is generally safe for use in children 9 years of age and older under the supervision of a doctor. It is not recommended for children under 9. Elderly: No special dose adjustments are typically needed, but older adults should use with caution as aging skin may be more sensitive to irritation. Sensitive Skin: If you have eczema, rosacea, or very sensitive skin, speak to your doctor before starting this medication.
